help_text.const: Alignment represents your character's moral and ethical outlook. It's a guide for roleplaying, not a strict rule. Most adventuring parties work best with good or neutral alignments.

champion.description: Champions must follow alignments compatible with their deity

help_text.const: Clerics and Champions must choose a deity, as their powers come from divine worship. Other classes may choose to worship a deity for roleplay purposes.

alignment_compatibility.description: When enabled, enforces Pathfinder 2E rule: Character alignment must be within one step of deity alignment on both the Law-Chaos axis and Good-Evil axis (e.g., a Neutral Good deity allows LG, NG, CG, LN, N, CN followers).

error_message.const: Clerics and Champions must choose a deity. Your alignment must be within one step of your deity's alignment.

default: Alignment is a roleplaying tool, not a straitjacket. Your character can act in complex ways within their alignment.
Evil alignments are generally not recommended for new players or most campaigns.
Your deity choice can unlock special abilities and flavor for divine characters.
Clerics can use their deity's favored weapon with proficiency, even if it's normally outside their class proficiencies.
You can change alignment during play if your character's actions consistently reflect a different worldview.
